item.title: Grand Theft Auto 6's map is significantly larger than Rockstar's previous games; here's how it compares to the studio's other titles.
item.description: Grand Theft Auto 6's map is significantly larger than the maps in Rockstar's previous games. Here's how it compares to the studio's other titles, according to the developer. Rockstar Games confirmed to The New York Times and YouTuber TGG that Grand Theft Auto 6's map is three times bigger than the playable area of Red Dead Redemption 2. Elaborating to TGG, it was revealed that it is twice the size of Grand Theft Auto 5, and Vice City itself is twice the size of Los Santos from GTA 5. Vice City and its surrounding suburbs are 11 times bigger than Los Santos and its surrounding areas. If that wasn't enough for you, TGG also revealed that there are "hundreds" of accessible interiors in GTA 6. In GTA 5, players could enter the homes of their respective characters, different shops, and a few random buildings like the Los Santos police station, but generally speaking, there weren't a lot of places you could enter. GTA Online has added more over time, but they often require loading screens and are very restrictive. The GTA 6 extended look already showed off a variety of interiors both inside and outside of missions, so that should make Leonida a lot more layered. Speaking to IGN, Rockstar Games' Rob Nelson discussed how the developer took lessons learned from building Red Dead Redemption 2's version of the Wild West and expanded upon those ideas with GTA 6.

item.title: The official Pokémon profile on X has responded after its account was hacked by an unknown party who shared a post linking out to a memecoin.
item.description: The official Pokémon profile on X has responded after its account was hacked by an unknown party who shared a post linking out to a memecoin. The hack occurred around 3 PM PT on August 17, 2026. The post — which has since been deleted — was cleverly structured, appearing as an official Pokémon advertisement with a link to a site that, at first glance, looked like a legitimate page celebrating the brand’s 30th anniversary, which is ongoing. “Celebrate 30 years of Pokémon in a whole new way!” the post read. “Introducing $POKEMON, the official Pokemon memecoin. Join trainers around the world and be part of the #Pokemon30 celebration.” The post was up for around thirty minutes before it was finally taken down. Most commenters weren’t fooled, though, and it wasn’t long before proposed community notes began appearing underneath the supposed scam on X.

item.title: Rockstar Games has finally revealed an official look at GTA 6 gameplay, and members of the development team couldn't be happier to finally see fans' reactions.
item.description: Rockstar Games has finally revealed an official look at Grand Theft Auto 6 gameplay, and members of the development team couldn't be happier to finally see fans' reactions. Our first real glimpse at what the GTA 6 studio has been cooking up finally arrived as part of the Netflix extended look today. While there's still plenty of side activities, romance subplots, and robberies for Jason and Lucia that we've yet to see, the developers at Rockstar are just happy their work can be shown off as intended. "Our Teams across the World have worked incredibly hard," production designer Terrance Radcliff said. "So proud of everyone. Watching this with coworkers as a Family – and when I get home I’ll watch again with my Family!" "The first ever game I have played was Vice City as a kid," graphic programmer Mert Kirimgeri said. "It's an honour to be working with the most professional, brilliant and kind people on the planet over the most immersive game ever made, not to mention one of the most complex computer systems in human existence. Enjoy!!!"

item.title: Star Citizen single-player spinoff Squadron 42 has been delayed to 2027, with developer Chris Roberts insisting it wouldn't get the attention it deserves because of Grand Theft Auto 6.
item.description: Star Citizen single-player spinoff Squadron 42 has been delayed to 2027, with developer Chris Roberts insisting it wouldn't get the attention it deserves because of Grand Theft Auto 6. In a new blog post, Cloud Imperium Games CEO Chris Roberts announced that Squadron 42 will be launching in Q2 2027. The studio had previously announced 2026 as its release window and reaffirmed late last year that it was still targeting that. However, Roberts noted that GTA 6 is going to suck up all of the attention this fall, and as a result, it doesn't make sense to launch a new game during that time. "At CitizenCon 2024, we announced we would ship in 2026. Our plan was to release in Q4 around IAE," said Roberts. "But much like the rest of the industry there is no way I want to launch my spiritual successor to Wing Commander, a game that has had twelve years of blood, sweat and tears invested into it (we started Squadron 42 development in 2014 as 2013 was opening studios, hiring people and getting the Hangar module out for Star Citizen) launching into the attention buzz saw of GTA 6. While GTA 6 isn’t launching on PC this November, pretty much all outlets and most content creators will be all over it, not leaving a lot of room for other coverage." Roberts went on to note that CIG will be doing previews of Squadron 42 with content creators and early backers in October, which it will use as an opportunity to announce release plans with a concrete date to follow "shortly" afterwards. Q2 would place Squadron 42 sometime during the spring, so long as nothing changes between now and then.

item.title: Grand Theft Auto 6 will take a while for players to finish, with the game's producer stating it took him 80 hours.
item.description: Grand Theft Auto 6 will take a while for players to finish, with the game's producer stating it took him 80 hours. In an The New York Times interview, Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson revealed that it took him about 80 hours to finish the game in February. He noted that included the main story and some "optional goals with narrative ramifications," it's unclear if that included just mucking about in the open world or anything, though. Still, that is a sizable length regardless. Nelson ultimately hopes fans take their time with the game and don't rush through it. For comparison, GTA 4 and 5 are around 30 hours long, while Red Dead Redemption 2 is around 50-60 hours. So, that means GTA 6 will be the longest of Rockstar's games to date, which will be reassuring for fans who have waited a long time for this game. Assuming 80 hours doesn't include the time for 100% completion, there will still be plenty of ways to extend your time with the game. Grand Theft Auto 6 has no shortage of open-world activities, including basketball, fishing, exercising, and much more. There will also likely be a plethora of side missions for players to indulge in, so it seems like we'll all be playing GTA 6 for a long time. Red Dead Redemption 2 has kept players very active thanks to its level of depth and detail, thanks to unique NPCs, hidden details, and side content.

item.title: GTA 6 has a whole relationship system to increase Jason and Lucia’s bond, but it’s completely optional if you’d rather keep things platonic.
item.description: During an interview with IGN, Rob Nelson, the head of development and co-studio head at Rockstar North, explained the design decisions behind making Jason and Lucia's relationship key to the story but not to the gameplay mechanics. "I have to say it feels great — if you are into it as a concept. Don’t bother with it if you aren’t. Up to you," said Nelson. Jason and Lucia will always have each other's backs in the story and during the action, but spending quality time together and nurturing the relationship? That's up to the player, and you won't be penalized if you're not interested in the sappy stuff. "The narrative is structured in such a way that the circumstances they find themselves in require them to stay together for most of the story and work together. At the very least they will get through most things as partners in crime," explained Nelson. "I don’t want to say too much more about this because I don’t want to spoil anything. It really adds a compelling element to things, and it’s one of the reasons we wanted to approach this sort of story, because it's completely different for us. Could we bring some sort of emotional resonance to GTA for people if they wanted to engage with it? Could we also provide mechanisms for people to just opt out of it if they're not into it? If they feel like, ‘I don't want a relationship in this?’ That's what we're going to find out. It's not something that we want to foist upon players."

item.title: We asked Rockstar how it’s dealing with the pressure of ensuring GTA 6 is a success after so many years of development: ‘We are nervous!’
item.description: It feels like the whole world is waiting to play GTA 6. And Rockstar knows it. Ahead of the extended look that just debuted on Netflix, IGN had the chance to visit the developer and talk with Rob Nelson, co-studio head at Rockstar North. Upon us mentioning just how each new Grand Theft Auto feels like a global cultural moment, he replies with a laugh, “No pressure.” “I try not to think about it,” Nelson continues. “You’re aware of it, of course. But I think we just have to try and make something that we feel is innovating on what we’ve done previously, evolving it while still making it feel familiar.” Rockstar knows that each and every scrap of information revealed about GTA 6 is analysed with a fine-tooth comb, and this recent extended look is certainly no different, as we’re given our biggest insight yet into the world, characters, and gameplay of this revisit to Vice City. It means each frame needs to be perfect, with every detail bound to be made into a list feature revealing new secrets about the game — exactly something we’ll be doing ourselves.

item.title: Following GTA 5’s three playable characters, Rockstar considered putting four protagonists in GTA 6 before settling on its criminal couple.
item.description: Long before we knew that GTA 6 would be played from the perspective of dual protagonists Jason and Lucia, many were wondering just how many playable characters Rockstar’s latest would include. And it turns out that the answer wasn’t always two. Grand Theft Auto 5 charted a new direction for the series by increasing the number of characters to three, where there had always been just one. Red Dead Redemption 2 does have multiple protagonists, but can never be switched between in the style of GTA 5 due to story reasons. It begged the question of which direction the developer would go when first designing 6. IGN recently visited Rockstar North to speak with co-studio head Rob Nelson, who revealed discussions were had at one point in time regarding the number of characters increasing to four. But, ultimately, the team landed on one couple, with the bonds built between player and character at the foremost point of those discussions. “As the narrative unfolds, we're quite conscious to try and make sure that players have enough time with each character,” says Nelson. “After doing GTA 5, we talked about different ideas of – do we do more characters? How do we follow up three characters? Is it four characters now? But we worried about diluting the amount of player time with each and therefore player connection with those characters. So we decided to step in this direction of two characters in a relationship.”

item.title: Rockstar explains how it has pushed current-gen technology to ensure GTA 6’s massive map is a step beyond Red Dead Redemption 2’s world.
item.description: When it comes to open-world games, and especially Rockstar’s, one of the biggest questions is always “how big is the map?” Well, when it comes to GTA 6 we now have a answer. Kind of. The main stories of Rockstar games and the bombastic missions that they’re made up of are always a huge part of the allure of these now once-in-a-generation events, but there’s always plenty to do once those tales have ended. As with 2018’s Red Dead Redemption 2, it will be no different in GTA 6. “There is a whole other world in Red Dead Redemption 2, yes. GTA 6 is very much like that,” Rob Nelson, co-studio head of Rockstar North, told IGN in an exclusive interview. “There's a whole lot of stuff that you discover emergently that we're not necessarily directing you to through objectives or blips or icons on a map as well. If you take a bit of time and explore you will be rewarded – a lot. It’s a big map, a very big map.” To create such a large playground to play in takes a huge amount of time and effort, though, as well as the tools to build them with. This is where the power of the current generation of consoles comes into the picture, with Rockstar now able to push things even further than Red Dead Redemption 2 was able to go when it launched on PS4 and Xbox One.

item.title: CD Projekt Red enlisted the help of a modder to help make the newly revealed The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt – Remastered look better than ever.
item.description: CD Projekt Red enlisted the help of a well-known modder to help make the newly revealed The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt – Remastered look better than ever. The community creator, who calls themselves HalkHogan, shared the news in an update post on the Nexus Mods page for their own The Witcher 3 HD Rework Project (HDRP) mod. This single PC mod alone has garnered more than 320,000 unique downloads and more than 1.6 million views, and it sounds like it caught CD Projekt Red's attention ahead of The Witcher 3 Remastered, too. In their message, HalkHogan confirmed their involvement in CD Projekt Red's official remaster release, telling fans of their work that they'll no longer need to use HDRP. Instead, they suggest players check out their contributions in The Witcher 3 Remastered, instead. "Hello, my Witcher friends!" the message reads. "It's been a while since the last news, and I would like to clarify any questions and confirm that I am cooperating with CDPR on the Witcher 3 Remaster, and my work will be officially available in the game on September 29th (on PC and consoles). HDRP will no longer be needed."

item.title: The lore of Kingdom Hearts is so expansive that Tetsuya Nomura says Square Enix hired a loremaster to keep its story cohesive.
item.description: The lore of Kingdom Hearts is so expansive that Tetsuya Nomura says Square Enix hired a loremaster to keep its story cohesive. Kingdom Hearts IV is officially set for a late 2027 release. In the lead-up to its highly anticipated launch, fans have been returning to previous games in the series, to the point where a collection of Kingdom Hearts titles became one of the highest-selling games on Steam following an extended gameplay trailer shown at D23 in July. In total, there are 13 games in the Kingdom Hearts franchise, which have been released on a bevy of different platforms over the years. That’s a lot to play through, not to mention a lot of story beats to keep track of as you go. This isn’t a player-specific problem; even the developers find themselves getting lost from time to time, as revealed by series creator Tetsuya Nomura during an August 2026 interview with Famitsu. In fact, the storyline is so convoluted that Square Enix hired a loremaster to keep everything cohesive and explain the plot to Disney.

item.title: Panic's Playdate, a crank-powered handheld gaming system, launched all the way back in 2022, but last year it fell victim to the same tariffs that hit many gaming products. And, now that the Supreme Court has ordered the government to refund those fees, Panic is forwarding those refunds to the customers that actually paid them.
item.description: Panic's Playdate, a crank-powered handheld gaming system, launched all the way back in 2022, but last year it got hit with the same tariffs as many gaming products. Now that the Supreme Court has ordered the government to refund those fees, Panic is forwarding those refunds to the customers that actually paid them. The company started sending out emails, spotted on LinkedIn and Reddit, informing customers that they'd be getting a tariff refund sent to their original payment method. The refund itself isn't much — the highest one I've seen is a $25 refund — but when it's attached to a handheld that costs $250 now and $179 at launch, it's a pretty decent percentage. If you bought one of these fun little handhelds when the tariffs were active, you should be automatically getting an email notifying you of the refund. If not, you should be able to reach out to help@play.date to figure out what's going on. Ideally, we'd see more companies refunding tariffs now that the refunds have started flowing from the governmen, but there are definitely companies that are holding on to those fees. Even Nintendo has refused to issue refunds to Switch 2 customers, arguing that gamers got exactly what they paid for. Hopefully, the Playdate manufacturers can set a decent example for other companies to follow.

item.title: FromSoftware has delivered a surprise Elden Ring update, revealing the biggest changes its critically acclaimed action-RPG has gotten in years.
item.description: FromSoftware has delivered a surprise Elden Ring update, revealing the biggest changes its critically acclaimed action-RPG has gotten in years. The developer caught fans off-guard with lengthy patch notes today, detailing a list of buffs (and a few nerfs) for different weapons and playstyles across the game. It's a major update that arrived as FromSoftware prepares for the launch of Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition for Nintendo Switch 2, as well as its accompanying DLC for other platforms. What we have here is a laundry list of balance adjustments that get under the hood to tweak a variety of PvE and PvP tools. Based on the list of updates available on the Dark Souls developer's website, the last time we received patch notes of a similar length was back in October 2024, a few months after the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion released. That makes it not only one of the biggest updates the 2022 game-of-the-year winner has received in years, but what could be one of its final ones, too. Generally, what Elden Ring players have to look forward to is a lot of buffs. The Firespark, Lightning, Chilling, Frenzyflame, and Deadly Poison Perfume Bottles, for example, got increased attack power across the board. The Smithscript Axe and Spear, as well as the Spear of the Impaler, also benefit from reduced stamina use and increased power for thrown attacks.

item.title: Pretty much everyone expects the November launch of GTA 6 to dominate the world of entertainment — indeed that’s one of the reasons we have a September crush of video game releases. But according to the CEO of Helldivers 2 developer Arrowhead, there are two very good reasons why developers shouldn’t be too worried.
item.description: Pretty much everyone expects the November launch of GTA 6 to dominate the world of entertainment — indeed that’s one of the reasons we have a September crush of video game releases. But according to the CEO of Helldivers 2 developer Arrowhead, there are two very good reasons why developers shouldn’t be too worried. Speaking to IGN, Arrowhead boss Shams Jorjani said that the lack of a PC version of GTA 6 at launch, as well as the absence of whatever the next generation of GTA Online looks like, means there’s reason to believe games like Helldivers 2 retain their own space. “Rockstar makes ridiculous, high-effort stuff and it's awesome that games like this get made,” Jorjani said. “On a selfish level I'm happy it’s not hitting PC right away, and that online isn’t dropping at launch. It means Helldivers 2 gets to keep crushing it in our own space, and is also why it won’t be the all consuming behemoth everyone’s worried about. “Everyone in the industry right now is constantly pivoting strategies and obsessing over early player feedback just to survive. But Rockstar has the brand power to confidently take their time and run their classic play. They have the confidence and freedom to spend a decade doing things the old-school way because they know the core game will deliver. It’s going to raise the bar for sure.”

item.title: Florida officials and Rockstar Games are having conversations to turn parts of Miami into Vice City for Grand Theft Auto 6's marketing campaign.
item.description: Florida officials and Rockstar Games are having conversations to turn parts of Miami into Vice City for Grand Theft Auto 6's marketing campaign. As initially reported by The Miamian, Miami-Dade County has had formal conversations with Rockstar Games about a Grand Theft Auto 6-themed takeover of Miami to promote the upcoming game. The report initially noted that Rockstar was the one that approached Miami-Dade with its ideas, but the article was later edited to clarify the city was actually the one who submitted a pitch deck. While no plans are officially in place yet, the ideas pitched by the city are wide-ranging, ambitious, and likely absurdly expensive. One such idea includes transforming a section of Miami International Airport to serve as a "welcome" area for Vice City, complete with Vice City signage, limited edition luggage tags, themed luggage carts, a photo backdrop, and even a display aircraft wrapped in the game's purple color scheme. Officials also proposed various activations around Miami's beaches, parks, and ports, creating unique events with DJs, food, exotic vehicles, photo ops, drone shows, murals, and much more. Outside of actual events, there are even ideas to have Rockstar take over the city's busses and trains with Vice City branding on the actual locomotives and stations associated with them. On the smaller side, there was also a pitch for Vice City-branded manhole covers and utility boxes.

item.title: State of Decay 3 fans will have the chance to play the game later this year via a closed beta.
item.description: State of Decay 3 fans will have the chance to play the game later this year via a closed beta. Undead Labs has confirmed that it will hold a closed beta for State of Decay 3 before the end of 2026. Exact dates weren't given, but interested fans can sign up now by clicking here and filling out the required information. The studio also held an alpha earlier this year, which reportedly resulted in actionable feedback to improve the game. The team noted that the alpha allowed them to improve combat, cosmetics, visuals, and movement, resulting in a better product. The beta will only allow more opportunities to improve the game, according to Undead Labs. “We’re going to be expanding our alpha and then closed beta to more players over time, this is our largest map ever and with untethered multiplayer, we really need to take the opportunities to stress-test and fine-tune,” said Kevin Patzelt, Creative Director at Undead Labs. “If you don’t get access right away, rest assured there will be more opportunities throughout the year for players familiar and brand new to the series.” State of Decay 3 has been in the works since at least 2020, when the game was announced at the Xbox Series X/S reveal event. The project went quiet for a number of years, but was re-revealed in 2024 and is now planned for release sometime in 2027. It's been a long road, and it hasn't been an easy one. Undead Labs is also splitting away from Xbox, as part of the platform's big reset. Xbox underwent a massive restructuring earlier this summer, leading to extensive layoffs and multiple studios being sold off or released to go independent.
